items.title: kick-foot-not-visible
items.claim: In Image #4, the raised leg under FRONT KICK ends at a trouser cuff with no visible foot, whereas Image #22 shows a bare foot during the same named technique.
items.reason: The foot helps players read the strike’s reach, but these stills cannot establish whether the difference comes from animation phase, artwork, or texture clipping.
items.suggest: Capture the pose ID, animation phase, and atlas UVs matching Image #4; inspect that exact source cell and repair any confirmed foot clipping rather than changing the whole kick animation.

items.title: unmapped-stick-directions
items.claim: In Image #15, both sticks show directional chevrons and STANCE or TECHNIQUE labels, but no visible direction-to-action mapping.
items.reason: The control names alone do not tell a player which direction produces a punch, kick, jump, or crouch.
items.suggest: Keep readable action labels beside the corresponding stick directions, using the mapping already displayed in Image #3 and adjusting layout rather than shrinking text.

items.title: opening-card-omits-goal
items.claim: The opening card in Image #2 explains combining technique and stance inputs but does not state the first-to-two-points objective described in Image #6.
items.reason: Players see how to issue a move before seeing what wins the round.
items.suggest: Add a short rule beneath the input instruction: “One clean contact ends the exchange. First to 2 points wins.”

items.title: score-call-needs-translation
items.claim: Image #20 pairs a half-point scoreboard value with WAZA-ARI, but the callout does not explicitly say HALF POINT.
items.reason: The scoreboard and callout agree, but players unfamiliar with the terminology must decode that relationship themselves.
items.suggest: Add HALF POINT beneath WAZA-ARI and FULL POINT beneath IPPON while retaining the existing technique name.

items.title: winner-heading-wrap-varies
items.claim: ASMONGOLD WINS occupies two lines in Image #18, while HASANABI WINS occupies one line in Image #8.
items.reason: The same result hierarchy changes with the winner’s name, making the score’s placement less consistent.
items.suggest: Give both result headings the same two-line structure: fighter name first, WINS second, without reducing the font size.
